elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: New Section 10.9: "commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: New Section 10.9: "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: New Section 10.9: "where HDI processes any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000" — the trigger covers every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer rather than selected named data types.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: New Section 10.9: "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: New Section 10.9: "HDI shall provide certificates of insurance to the Company on request".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O of "not less than $2,000,000" exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability of "not less than $5,000,000" exceeds USD 2,000,000; the processing condition applies here because HDI hosts the Site and handles Company Content and user/order information (Sections 1.4, 1.5, 8.1).

reasons: The insertion is a single new Section 10.9 in General Provisions; no existing wording in Sections 10.1–10.8 was deleted or paraphrased, so no favourable retained language is disturbed.

The drafter correctly omitted the model language's non-checklist extras — the "at its own expense" qualifier and the "one (1) year thereafter" survival tail — keeping the insertion to exactly the six preferred elements.

All six preferred elements appear in operative language with the correct amounts, bases (per occurrence vs aggregate) and party direction (HDI as the insuring party), so the preferred level is position-complete; the fallback floors are satisfied a fortiori.
The cyber trigger is drafted to the full data-category standard ("any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company") rather than to selected named data types.

No undefined terms, dangling cross-references or contradictory retained sentences are created; the clause is free-standing and does not disturb allocation, timing, remedies or commercial mechanics elsewhere in the Agreement.
